## `apple.permission-purpose-string` — Permission purpose strings are present and specific

Checks every NS*UsageDescription key in the app's Info.plist (and Expo ios.infoPlist) for empty or vague text, and flags keys that a direct dependency needs but the app does not declare.

- **Version:** 0.1.0 (introduced in 0.1.0)
- **Frameworks:** flutter, react-native, expo, native-ios
- **Category:** permissions
- **Requirement status:** verified; last verified 2026-10-14
- **Fix:** Give every purpose string a specific sentence that explains which feature uses the data and why. Remove keys for features the app does not have.
- **Sources:**
  - [App Review Guidelines 5.1.1 – Data Collection and Storage](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/#data-collection-and-storage)
  - [Information Property List (purpose strings / usage descriptions)](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/information-property-list)
- **Limitations:**
  - The vagueness check is a heuristic for English text; localized strings are only checked for being empty or too short.
  - Dependency-to-key mapping covers popular Flutter and React Native plugins; other SDKs may need keys the scanner does not know.
  - Expo managed projects get purpose strings from config plugins at prebuild, so missing-key checks are skipped there.

## `apple.required-reason-api` — Required reason APIs are declared in the privacy manifest

Finds required reason APIs (UserDefaults, file timestamps, system boot time, disk space, active keyboards) in app-owned Swift/Objective-C code, then checks PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy declares each category with an approved reason code and is part of the Xcode project.

- **Version:** 0.1.0 (introduced in 0.1.0)
- **Frameworks:** flutter, react-native, native-ios
- **Category:** privacy
- **Requirement status:** verified; last verified 2026-10-14
- **Fix:** Add PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy to the app target and declare every required reason API category your own code uses, with the approved reason that matches the use.
- **Sources:**
  - [Describing use of required reason API](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/describing-use-of-required-reason-api)
  - [Privacy manifest files](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/privacy-manifest-files)
- **Limitations:**
  - API usage is detected by symbol names in source code, so wrappers, macros or generated code can be missed or over-matched.
  - Third-party SDKs are responsible for their own privacy manifests; they are not checked by this rule.
  - Approved reason codes come from Apple's documentation as fetched on 2026-10-14.

## `google.account-deletion-web` — Web link for account deletion requests is declared

For apps that appear to support account creation, checks that a public web URL for account deletion requests is declared in .release-doctor.yml, as Google Play requires one in the Data safety form.

- **Version:** 0.1.0 (introduced in 0.1.0)
- **Frameworks:** flutter, react-native, expo, native-android
- **Category:** account-lifecycle
- **Requirement status:** verified; last verified 2026-10-14
- **Applies when:** account_creation_detected_or_declared
- **Fix:** Publish a page where users can request deletion of their account and data without the app installed, and enter it in the Data safety form.
- **Sources:**
  - [Understanding Google Play's app account deletion requirements](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13327111) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
  - [Provide information for Google Play's Data safety section](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
- **Limitations:**
  - The scanner cannot read Play Console; it relies on app.account_deletion.web_url.
  - URLs are not fetched because scans run offline.

## `google.sensitive-permissions` — Sensitive Android permissions have a policy path

Lists permissions in src/main manifests (and Expo android.permissions) that Google Play restricts or requires a declaration for, and the permissions whose data must appear in the Data safety form.

- **Version:** 0.1.0 (introduced in 0.1.0)
- **Frameworks:** flutter, react-native, expo, native-android
- **Category:** permissions
- **Requirement status:** verified; last verified 2026-10-14
- **Fix:** Remove sensitive permissions the app does not need (use tools:node="remove" for ones merged from libraries) and prepare Play Console declarations for the rest.
- **Sources:**
  - [Permissions and APIs that Access Sensitive Information](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9888170) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
  - [Requesting access to location in the background](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9799150) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
  - [Use of SMS or Call Log permission groups](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10208820) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
  - [Use of All files access (MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE) permission](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10467955) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
  - [Use of the broad package (app) visibility (QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES) permission](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10158779) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
  - [Google Play's Photo and Video Permissions policy](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/14115180) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
  - [Understanding foreground service and full-screen intent requirements](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13392821) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
  - [Provide information for Google Play's Data safety section](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
- **Limitations:**
  - Permissions added by library manifests during the manifest merge are not visible; inspect the merged manifest of a release build.
  - Whether a use qualifies as core functionality is a human judgement.

## `google.target-api-level` — targetSdk meets Google Play's current requirement

Reads targetSdk from the app module (or uses-sdk / expo-build-properties) and compares it with the requirement effective on the scan date, taken from the versioned policy snapshot.

- **Version:** 0.1.0 (introduced in 0.1.0)
- **Frameworks:** flutter, react-native, expo, native-android
- **Category:** build-configuration
- **Requirement status:** verified; last verified 2026-10-14
- **Fix:** Raise targetSdk to the required API level after testing the behavior changes of each Android version you skip.
- **Sources:**
  - [Meet Google Play's target API level requirement](https://developer.android.com/google/play/requirements/target-sdk)
  - [Target API level requirements for Google Play apps (Play Console Help)](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/11926878) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
- **Limitations:**
  - Computed values (flutter.targetSdkVersion, version catalogs) are not evaluated and return needs_review.
  - Form factor is inferred from <uses-feature>; extension deadlines granted in Play Console are not known to the scanner.

## `shared.account-deletion-in-app` — Apps with account creation offer in-app account deletion

Looks for account-creation signals (auth SDKs, sign-up calls, sign-up labels or a developer declaration) and for an account deletion flow. Never passes on keywords alone; found flows are returned for manual verification.

- **Version:** 0.1.0 (introduced in 0.1.0)
- **Frameworks:** flutter, react-native, expo, native-ios, native-android
- **Category:** account-lifecycle
- **Requirement status:** verified; last verified 2026-10-14
- **Applies when:** account_creation_detected_or_declared
- **Fix:** Provide an easy-to-find in-app action that initiates deletion of the account and its associated data, and record its path in .release-doctor.yml.
- **Sources:**
  - [Offering account deletion in your app](https://developer.apple.com/support/offering-account-deletion-in-your-app/)
  - [App Review Guidelines 5.1.1 – Data Collection and Storage](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/#data-collection-and-storage)
  - [Understanding Google Play's app account deletion requirements](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13327111) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
- **Limitations:**
  - Keyword search cannot prove the flow is reachable or deletes server-side data.
  - Accounts created via web views or custom backends may not be detected; declare app.has_account_creation.

## `shared.app-identifier` — Application ID and bundle identifier are not template values

Validates the Android application ID and iOS bundle identifier format and flags the com.example prefix left by project templates.

- **Version:** 0.1.0 (introduced in 0.1.0)
- **Frameworks:** flutter, react-native, expo, native-ios, native-android
- **Category:** build-configuration
- **Requirement status:** verified; last verified 2026-10-14
- **Fix:** Use a reverse-domain identifier you own; it cannot be changed after the first release.
- **Sources:**
  - [Configure the app module (application ID)](https://developer.android.com/build/configure-app-module)
  - [App Review Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/)
- **Limitations:**
  - Identifiers set through build flavors or xcconfig files are not resolved.

## `shared.debug-configuration` — Release builds do not use debug configuration

Flags release builds signed with the debug key, debuggable release builds, global cleartext traffic on Android and globally disabled App Transport Security on iOS.

- **Version:** 0.1.0 (introduced in 0.1.0)
- **Frameworks:** flutter, react-native, native-ios, native-android, expo
- **Category:** build-configuration
- **Requirement status:** verified; last verified 2026-10-14
- **Fix:** Sign release builds with your own upload key and keep debug-only settings out of release configuration.
- **Sources:**
  - [Sign your app](https://developer.android.com/studio/publish/app-signing)
  - [Security risk: android:debuggable](https://developer.android.com/privacy-and-security/risks/android-debuggable)
  - [Security risk: cleartext communications](https://developer.android.com/privacy-and-security/risks/cleartext-communications)
  - [NSAppTransportSecurity](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/information-property-list/nsapptransportsecurity)
- **Limitations:**
  - Signing set up only in CI (environment variables, injected properties) is not visible.
  - Per-build-type Info.plist files and xcconfig overrides are not resolved.

## `shared.embedded-secrets` — No credentials embedded in the project

Scans text files for private keys, cloud and payment API secrets, signing passwords and credential files, using git tracking status to separate committed files from local ones. Values are always redacted.

- **Version:** 0.1.0 (introduced in 0.1.0)
- **Frameworks:** flutter, react-native, expo, native-ios, native-android
- **Category:** security
- **Requirement status:** verified; last verified 2026-10-14
- **Fix:** Remove credentials from the project and git history, rotate them, and keep privileged operations on your backend.
- **Sources:**
  - [App Review Guidelines 5.1.1 – Data Collection and Storage](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/#data-collection-and-storage)
  - [User Data policy (privacy policy requirements)](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10144311) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
- **Limitations:**
  - Generic credential-like assignments are a heuristic and return warn, never fail.
  - Public client identifiers (Firebase / Google API keys) are reported as info, not as leaks.
  - Git history is not scanned; only the current working tree.

## `shared.permission-usage-evidence` — Declared permissions have a matching feature

For each declared capability (camera, location, photos, contacts, microphone, Bluetooth, ...), looks for a dependency or API call that uses it. Declared permissions with no evidence are returned for review.

- **Version:** 0.1.0 (introduced in 0.1.0)
- **Frameworks:** flutter, react-native, expo, native-ios, native-android
- **Category:** permissions
- **Requirement status:** needs-research; last verified 2026-10-14
- **Fix:** Confirm which feature uses each permission and remove permissions and purpose strings that no feature needs.
- **Sources:**
  - [App Review Guidelines 5.1.1 – Data Collection and Storage](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/#data-collection-and-storage)
  - [Permissions and APIs that Access Sensitive Information](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9888170) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
- **Limitations:**
  - Absence of evidence is not proof that a permission is unused; plugins and native SDKs may use it indirectly.
  - Only known dependencies and common API names are recognized.

## `shared.placeholder-content` — No template or placeholder content

Looks for framework starter templates, lorem ipsum, "Coming soon" labels and template launcher labels that suggest an incomplete app.

- **Version:** 0.1.0 (introduced in 0.1.0)
- **Frameworks:** flutter, react-native, expo, native-ios, native-android
- **Category:** app-completeness
- **Requirement status:** needs-research; last verified 2026-10-14
- **Fix:** Replace placeholder content and hide unfinished features in release builds.
- **Sources:**
  - [App Review Guidelines 2.1 – App Completeness](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/#app-completeness)
  - [App Review Guidelines 4.2 – Minimum Functionality](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/#minimum-functionality)
  - [Spam and Minimum Functionality policy](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9898783) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
- **Limitations:**
  - A match does not mean the text is reachable in the release build.
  - Screens, images and runtime behavior are not inspected.

## `shared.privacy-policy` — Privacy policy is available and covers detected SDKs

Finds the privacy policy URL (config, fastlane metadata, app code) or a policy document in the repository, flags placeholder URLs, and compares a local policy document with data-collecting SDKs found in dependencies.

- **Version:** 0.1.0 (introduced in 0.1.0)
- **Frameworks:** flutter, react-native, expo, native-ios, native-android
- **Category:** privacy
- **Requirement status:** verified; last verified 2026-10-14
- **Fix:** Link a public privacy policy in both store listings and inside the app, and make sure it describes the data each SDK collects.
- **Sources:**
  - [App Review Guidelines 5.1.1 – Data Collection and Storage](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/#data-collection-and-storage)
  - [App privacy details on the App Store](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/app-privacy-details/)
  - [User Data policy (privacy policy requirements)](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10144311) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
  - [Provide information for Google Play's Data safety section](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469) _(URL not yet re-fetched by a maintainer)_
- **Limitations:**
  - Store consoles are not visible; a policy entered only there produces needs_review.
  - The SDK comparison checks for vendor names or purposes in the text, not legal adequacy.
  - The scanner does not assume an SDK collects every data type it can collect.

## `shared.release-version` — Version name and build number are valid and consistent

Validates the app version (pubspec.yaml, Gradle, Info.plist, Xcode build settings, Expo app.json) against store format rules and flags hard-coded values that override the Flutter source of truth.

- **Version:** 0.1.0 (introduced in 0.1.0)
- **Frameworks:** flutter, react-native, expo, native-ios, native-android
- **Category:** build-configuration
- **Requirement status:** verified; last verified 2026-10-14
- **Fix:** Keep one source of truth for the version and increase the build number for every upload.
- **Sources:**
  - [CFBundleShortVersionString](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/information-property-list/cfbundleshortversionstring)
  - [Version your app](https://developer.android.com/studio/publish/versioning)
- **Limitations:**
  - Values injected by CI (fastlane, --build-number flags) are not visible.
  - Does not know the last uploaded build number, so it cannot check that the number increased.

## `shared.review-access` — Reviewers can access account-based features

When the app appears to have accounts or the developer declares that login is needed, checks that a working demo account for App Review and Play Console App access has been confirmed in .release-doctor.yml.

- **Version:** 0.1.0 (introduced in 0.1.0)
- **Frameworks:** flutter, react-native, expo, native-ios, native-android
- **Category:** store-metadata
- **Requirement status:** verified; last verified 2026-10-14
- **Applies when:** login_required_or_accounts_detected
- **Fix:** Provide reviewers with a non-expiring demo account (or a full demo mode) in App Store Connect and Play Console App access, and test it first.
- **Sources:**
  - [App Review Guidelines 2.1 – App Completeness](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/#app-completeness)
- **Limitations:**
  - Store consoles are not visible; the rule relies on the developer's declaration.
  - Credentials are never read from or written to the config file.
